extracted.intended_audience: researchers, journal editors, publishers, repository and submission-system developers, and research administrators implementing contributor attribution
extracted.subtask_description: Applying the CRediT (Contributor Roles Taxonomy) vocabulary to indicate what each contributor to a scholarly research project actually did, and implementing its metadata in publication/submission systems. Covers role selection, optional degree-of-contribution labels, and machine-readable encoding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Ideas; formulation or evolution of overarching research goals and aims. Includes developing research questions, formulating hypotheses, and identifying gaps in existing knowledge that the research will address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: Development or design of methodology; creation of models. Encompasses designing experimental protocols, analytical frameworks, and theoretical models that guide the research process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software
rubrics_metrics.description: Programming, software development; designing computer programs; implementation of the computer code and supporting algorithms; testing of existing code components. Covers all computational tool development necessary for conducting or analyzing the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification, whether as a part of the activity or separate, of the overall replication/reproducibility of results/experiments and other research outputs. Ensures research findings are reliable, replicable, and meet quality standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of statistical, mathematical, computational, or other formal techniques to analyze or synthesize study data. Includes all quantitative and qualitative analytical work performed on collected data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: Conducting a research and investigation process, specifically performing the experiments, or data/evidence collection. The hands-on work of executing experiments, surveys, observations, and other data-gathering activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of study materials, reagents, materials, patients, laboratory samples, animals, instrumentation, computing resources, or other analysis tools. Providing the physical, biological, or computational resources necessary for the research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Curation
rubrics_metrics.description: Management activities to annotate (produce metadata), scrub data and maintain research data (including software code, where it is necessary for interpreting the data itself) for initial use and later re-use. Organizing, maintaining, and documenting data to ensure its long-term utility and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing – Original Draft
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work, specifically writing the initial draft (including substantive translation). Creating the first complete version of the manuscript or major sections thereof.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing – Review & Editing
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work by those from the original research group, specifically critical review, commentary or revision – including pre- or post-publication stages. Refining, revising, and improving the manuscript through editorial work and critical feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visualization
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparation, creation and/or presentation of the published work, specifically visualization/data presentation. Creating figures, charts, diagrams, and other visual elements that communicate research findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervision
rubrics_metrics.description: Oversight and leadership responsibility for the research activity planning and execution, including mentorship external to the core team. Providing guidance, mentorship, and strategic direction for the research project and team members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Administration
rubrics_metrics.description: Management and coordination responsibility for the research activity planning and execution. Handling logistics, timelines, communications, and organizational aspects of the research project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding Acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisition of the financial support for the project leading to this publication. Securing grants, contracts, or other funding sources that enable the research to be conducted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-hierarchical roles and multiplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: CRediT defines 14 distinct contributor roles organized into four functional categories, without hierarchy. Contributors can hold multiple roles, and not every role must be filled in every research project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree of contribution (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: CRediT provides for indicating the degree of contribution ("lead", "equal", or "supporting") for each contributor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The NISO standard describes degree-of-contribution labels as optional for CRediT users to implement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Machine‑readable metadata and unique role identifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: The CRediT standard includes machine-readable metadata. Each role has a unique identifier URL for use in structured metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementations should use the provided vocab-term-identifier URLs to enable precise machine-readable identification and linking. Example encodings include JATS XML with role vocab attributes; the vocab-term-identifier attribute provides a unique URL for each specific CRediT role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supported schema formats
rubrics_metrics.description: NISO provides technical specifications for representing CRediT data in multiple formats to ensure compatibility with diverse systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supported/encouraged formats include: XML Schema (especially JATS XML) for publication systems; JSON Schema for web apps/APIs; JSON-LD for linked data/knowledge graphs; and schema.org integration for discoverability (Google Scholar, knowledge graphs). Choose formats appropriate to your platform and use-case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open standard and licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: The taxonomy is an open standard conforming to the OpenStand Principles and is published under a CC-BY Creative Commons licence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CRediT role identifiers and metadata formats are intended for broad reuse and integration across publishers and systems; follow the license and OpenStand principles when reusing or extending CRediT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of CRediT (scope and reliability cautions)
rubrics_metrics.description: CRediT was originally created to be used for both byline authors and other contributors (acknowledgees), but most publishers have implemented it only for authors. Some contributions by acknowledgees may not be well-described by the categories, and the categories may be too coarse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Potential consequences include named authors attributing acknowledgee roles to themselves (creating misleading attributions). Studies show low inter-rater agreement on classifying contributions, and CRediT does not resolve questions about the quantity/quality thresholds for authorship. Therefore, CRediT should be used alongside (not as a replacement for) authorship guidelines and with awareness of implementation limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: CRediT is not a determination of authorship
rubrics_metrics.description: According to the CRediT website, "CRediT is not designed to determine authorship but to provide more information about the specific contributions of authors."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementers and users should not treat role assignment alone as satisfying authorship criteria; separate authorship policies (e.g., ICMJE) remain necessary.
